decisions.reason: SOL preserves the earthquake and the surging aura while improving the sentence flow.
SOL keeps the low, far-reaching reverberation in natural English.
The Korean says language has power; “Words” narrows the meaning.
SOL preserves the ancient Dragon and naturally renders reaching a realm no other race entered.
SOL drops the simultaneous timing marked by “그와 동시에”.
“Roars full of killing intent” preserves the source’s 살기.
SOL preserves the gathered forces and cold order in clearer prose.
BASE retains “soon,” matching the source’s 이내.
SOL preserves the steel, torn flesh, battle cries, and the Black Dragon’s unwavering gaze.
The source says he had already regained his composure; SOL drops “already.”
The source frames the legion’s losses as a concession; SOL states them categorically.
SOL keeps the outcome tied to whether one human lives or dies.
“Slowly cutting through” naturally preserves his gradual advance through the soldiers.
SOL intensifies a chill in one corner of his heart into being chilled to the core.
SOL makes Morgoth already ruler of every world, while the source says he will become that ruler.
The source includes a second explosive sound; SOL removes it.
“About to rain down” preserves the flames’ imminent attack.
“Spike of ice” and “intercepted” preserve the projectile and its action.
SOL preserves the deflected flames and the steam obscuring the area; the radius conveys the source’s extent.
SOL drops the Black Dragon’s gleaming eyes.
“Covered head to toe” naturally preserves 전신, and the fierce eyes remain.
“Roared” naturally conveys the source’s roar-like shout.
SOL preserves the thousands-strong suicide squad’s charge and arrival at the battlefield.
SOL keeps the charge toward their Alliance Leader and sole hope.
SOL preserves the awaited voice and keeps the first-person viewpoint.
“There he was” preserves the recognition in natural narration.
SOL drops the simultaneous timing of the wind blades’ arrival.
The source stresses that he knew their weakness exactly; SOL drops that emphasis.
SOL preserves that he knew a long greeting was ill-timed.
“Sent a dagger” naturally preserves the act of throwing it toward Johnson.
The source says the soldier lunged over Johnson’s shoulder; SOL changes the trajectory to an attack from behind.
“Would rightly be called” preserves the hidden-weapon comparison.
SOL preserves the helmet and head being shattered while tightening the phrasing.
“This is hell” naturally conveys the Korean idiom that nothing could be worse than hell.
The source is inferential—“that would have been so”—while SOL asserts “Of course they had.”
“Willingly” preserves 기꺼이 without adding BASE’s “without hesitation.”
SOL shifts the original present count of twenty Hunters into the past.
SOL preserves the damp clouds and uses the glossary’s Great War rendering.
“Those awful things” preserves the blunt reaction without changing its target.
SOL preserves the comparison to the strongest Death Knights and their A-rank classification.
The source calls each soldier powerful or formidable; “troublesome” changes the category.
“Didn’t know one thing yet” preserves the impending revelation.
SOL keeps the obstacle to reaching Morgoth without changing the meaning.
“Like a beam of light” preserves the source’s image without claiming literal light-speed travel.
SOL preserves the angled spear blade catching the attack on its flat.
SOL naturally preserves the internal energy poured into the spear and its trembling shaft.
“Beyond it” preserves the familiar face’s position without BASE’s awkward relative clause.
SOL preserves the decades-long acquaintance, his shock at seeing the comrade, and the seven familiar faces.
SOL preserves Morgoth’s description of them as Guardians who protect him.
SOL naturally preserves the contrast between Taekyung’s perception and the Grand Mage’s.
SOL preserves the emotions in the voice and the gradual settling that leaves anger.
The deletion is sound because SOL carries “leaving only one” into the preceding sentence.
SOL specifies “what we’d do,” which the source leaves as “that kind of thing.”
SOL preserves the contrast between the fists’ force and aura.
“They carried memories” naturally connects the fragment to the preceding sentence.
SOL adds that he thought the days might kill him; the source describes the days as painfully unbearable.
The deletion is covered by SOL’s next sentence, which says the shattered pieces flew in every direction.
SOL preserves the scattered weapons and armor and bodies while making the action explicit.
“Old soldier” naturally conveys the veteran sense of 노장 in this battle scene.
SOL preserves the grief and anger in the roar.
“Why couldn’t they keep” naturally preserves the source’s question about failing to keep the promise.
The source says no voice answered his questions; SOL weakens this to answering him.
SOL adds that the old comrades advanced beneath the magic; the source only says they advanced.
SOL preserves both the lightning strike and the charging Guardians and soldiers.
SOL preserves the seemingly unstoppable force in natural English.
“They didn’t break through” preserves the contrast with the seemingly unstoppable charge.
“Joined in it” naturally preserves the many voices filling the spell.
SOL preserves Magic Johnson leading humanity’s greatest mages behind its only Grand Mage.
SOL drops the sudden appearance marked by 불현듯.
SOL makes explicit that the two spells canceled each other, as the context and source indicate.
“Began shaking space again” preserves the onset expressed by 시작하는.
“One thing was different” preserves the transition without changing its meaning.
The source introduces another group; SOL reduces that to unspecified additional faces.
“Tipped his head” naturally preserves the slight nod.
SOL preserves Felix’s dry refusal to apologize even if he was late.
SOL preserves the remembered, irritating manner of speaking in a complete sentence.
The source says Felix joined them; “arrived” loses that joining.
“Held back the heat” naturally preserves suppressing the feeling rising in his chest.
SOL preserves the seven Hunters fighting their old comrades as Taekyung moves on.
“One down, then another” preserves the repeated cutting action.
The short sentences preserve the relentless continuation without changing meaning.
BASE preserves the transitional beat before the strike; SOL moves the target ahead of that beat.
SOL deletes the monster phrase; BASE retains the source’s target and the glossary term.
The source says he stomped on empty air; SOL changes that physical action to treading.
